name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
kicker: 34th U.S. President · Supreme Allied Commander on D-Day
briefing: Dwight Eisenhower grew up in Abilene, Kansas, and as Supreme Allied Commander he led D-Day, the June 6, 1944, invasion of Normandy that helped free Western Europe from Nazi Germany. Elected the 34th president in 1952 with the slogan “I Like Ike,” he saw the fighting in Korea end, launched the Interstate Highway System, and sent troops to protect nine Black students at Little Rock’s Central High School.
answerHtml: Dwight D. Eisenhower (or Dwight David Eisenhower; accept Ike; prompt on Dwight)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: During World War I, this officer never reached the fighting in France; instead, he commanded Camp Colt, a tank training center at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania. Decades later, he retired to a farm next to the same battlefield.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this general who led the D-Day invasion and became the 34th president.

tossups.p: As a young officer, this man joined a 1919 Army truck convoy that took about two months to cross the country on poor roads, and in World War II he was impressed by Germany’s autobahns [“AW-toh-bahnz”].
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this president who signed the 1956 law that created the Interstate Highway System.

tossups.p: This general commanded Operation Torch, the Allied landings in Morocco and Algeria in November 1942. After American troops lost the Battle of Kasserine [“KASS-uh-reen”] Pass in Tunisia, he went on to oversee the Allied invasions of Sicily and Italy in 1943.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this American who next commanded the D-Day landings in Normandy as Supreme Allied Commander.

tossups.p: Before one invasion, this general wrote a note to be released if it failed, saying the blame was “mine alone.” His order of the day for that invasion told the troops, “You are about to embark upon the Great Crusade.”
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Supreme Allied Commander who launched the D-Day invasion of Normandy on June 6, 1944.

tossups.p: After World War II, this general wrote the memoir _Crusade in Europe_ and served as president of Columbia University. In 1951, he became the first Supreme Allied Commander Europe of NATO.
tossups.r: The next year, he won the presidency after promising, “I shall go to Korea.” For 10 points, name this 34th president.

tossups.p: This president signed the Civil Rights Act of 1957, the first federal civil rights law since Reconstruction, which created the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights. Senator Strom Thurmond spoke for more than 24 hours trying to block it.
tossups.r: That year, he also sent the 101st Airborne Division to protect nine Black students at Little Rock’s Central High. For 10 points, name this president.

tossups.p: After the Soviet Union launched the satellite Sputnik in 1957, the United States answered with Explorer 1 in 1958, and this president signed the National Defense Education Act to pay for more science, math, and foreign-language teaching.
tossups.r: In 1958, he also signed the law that created NASA. For 10 points, name this president who served from 1953 to 1961.

tossups.p: This president’s government at first claimed that a plane shot down over the Soviet Union in May 1960 was a weather research aircraft, until Nikita Khrushchev [“KROOSH-chef”] revealed that its pilot, Francis Gary Powers, had been captured alive.
tossups.r: In his 1961 farewell address, he warned against the “military-industrial complex.” For 10 points, name this president.

tossups.p: This president proposed “Atoms for Peace” in a 1953 speech to the United Nations, and at a 1955 summit in Geneva he offered an “Open Skies” plan to let the United States and the Soviet Union fly over each other’s territory.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Republican who had won the 1952 election by defeating Adlai Stevenson.

tossups.p: In 1954, this president explained his fear of communism spreading through Southeast Asia by comparing countries to a row of falling dominoes. That year, he decided not to send American forces to rescue the French at Dien Bien Phu [“DYEN BYEN FOO”].
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this president, who was in office when a 1953 armistice stopped the fighting in Korea.

tossups.p: During the Suez Crisis of 1956, this president pressured Britain, France, and Israel to pull their forces out of Egypt, whose leader, Gamal Abdel Nasser, had taken control of the Suez Canal.
tossups.r: The next year, he announced a doctrine promising U.S. help to Middle Eastern countries threatened by communism. For 10 points, name this president.

tossups.p: This man was born in Denison, Texas, grew up in Abilene, Kansas, and graduated from West Point in 1915, in a class later called “the class the stars fell on” because so many of its members became generals.
tossups.r: In 1952, his supporters’ buttons rhymed his nickname with the word “like.” For 10 points, name this general who became the 34th president.

tossups.p: This president named California governor Earl Warren Chief Justice in 1953, months before the Court heard new arguments in _Brown v. Board of Education_. He later appointed William Brennan and Potter Stewart to the Supreme Court.
tossups.r: In 1957, he sent federal troops to enforce school desegregation in Little Rock. For 10 points, name this president.

tossups.p: This president renamed the presidential retreat in Maryland’s Catoctin [“kuh-TOK-tin”] Mountains, which Franklin Roosevelt had called “Shangri-La,” in honor of his father and his grandson, both named David. He also had a putting green built near the Oval Office.
tossups.r: His vice president for eight years was Richard Nixon. For 10 points, name this 34th president.

tossups.p: This president created the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare in 1953 and welcomed Alaska and Hawaii as the 49th and 50th states in 1959. That same year, the St. Lawrence Seaway, which he had supported, opened to ships.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this president who signed the 1956 Federal-Aid Highway Act creating the Interstate Highway System.

trap.title: Ike, Truman, or MacArthur?
trap.body: Eisenhower’s career overlaps with two other famous names. Harry Truman was president from 1945 to 1953, so the atomic bombs, the Marshall Plan, and the start of the Korean War belong to Truman, while the 1953 armistice came after Eisenhower took office. Douglas MacArthur commanded in the Pacific and Korea, while Eisenhower led in North Africa and Europe; Eisenhower had once served as MacArthur’s aide. Terms named for him, like the Eisenhower Doctrine, are separate answers.
trap.fix: D-Day, Operation Torch, NATO’s first commander, “I Like Ike,” the interstates, Little Rock, NASA, the U-2, and the “military-industrial complex” all mean Eisenhower. Answer “Eisenhower” or “Ike”; if the question asks for “this doctrine,” say “Eisenhower Doctrine.”
trap.line: Real answer line: Dwight D. Eisenhower (or Dwight David Eisenhower; accept Ike)
